previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and a history of pseudoseizures was readmitted two days after discharge due to worsening left-sided abdominal pain, nausea with blood-tinged emesis, and syncope episodes triggered by pain. He had not taken his medications at home due to pain. Initial management included IV fluids, pain control, and NPO status. Labs and imaging showed no acute abdominal process. Psychiatric evaluation linked worsening nightmares and distress to discontinuation of ziprasidone, gabapentin, and cymbalta, recommending restarting gabapentin and ziprasidone, adding prazosin, and stopping amitriptyline. The patient improved with oral pain medication, advanced diet, and psychiatric medication adjustments. He was discharged home on hospital day two with stable pain, tolerating regular food, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
